routes.title: Nikko: a World Heritage shrine-and-temple walk
routes.introduction: Start at Tobu-Nikko Station, take the World Heritage bus to Shinkyo, then follow the historic precinct through Rinnoji, Toshogu, Futarasan Shrine and Taiyuin. Return to the station by bus from the Taiyuin/Futarasan stop. The mapped connectors show visit order only, not roads or walking paths.

stops.address: Shinkyo Bridge, Nikko, Tochigi, Japan
stops.story: Begin at the vermilion bridge over the Daiya River, the sacred threshold to Nikko's shrine-and-temple landscape. The bridge belongs to Futarasan-jinja and is part of the World Heritage site.

coordinates.precision: OpenStreetMap bridge way center

stops.story: At Sanbutsudo, Rinnoji's main hall, three large Buddha figures represent Nikko's sacred mountains. The temple precinct was founded by the monk Shodo.

coordinates.precision: OpenStreetMap Sanbutsudo way center

stops.name: Nikko Toshogu Shrine
stops.address: Nikko Toshogu Shrine, 2301 Sannai, Nikko, Tochigi, Japan
stops.story: Toshogu is the richly carved mausoleum shrine of Tokugawa Ieyasu. Give the precinct time: the famous Three Wise Monkeys and Yomeimon Gate are among many details along the visitor route.

stops.name: Nikko Futarasan-jinja Shrine

stops.story: Founded in 782, the shrine is dedicated to the deities of Nikko's three sacred mountains. Its main shrine grounds sit beside Toshogu and the forested temple precinct.

stops.story: Taiyuin is the mausoleum of Tokugawa Iemitsu. Its richly decorated gates and prayer hall honor his grandfather Ieyasu with a deliberately more restrained scale than Toshogu.

coordinates.precision: OpenStreetMap mausoleum way center

routes.title: Kawagoe: castle rooms to candy lane
routes.introduction: Start at Kawagoe Station and transfer toward Honmaru Goten by local bus or a longer walk. Then follow the historic town through the Kurazukuri merchant street, the ringing Toki no Kane and Kashiya Yokocho. The mapped sequence combines station access and walking; dashed connectors show stop order only, while the links open live directions for each leg.

coordinates.precision: Approximate station-area point from the existing Kawagoe route guide

stops.name: Kawagoe Castle Honmaru Goten
stops.address: Kawagoe Castle Honmaru Goten, 2-13-1 Kuruwa-machi, Kawagoe, Saitama 350-0053, Japan
stops.story: Built in 1848, this is the surviving entrance and great hall of Kawagoe Castle. Move slowly through its spare rooms and painted doors: this is a rare chance to imagine the everyday rhythm of a castle household rather than its battlefield image.

coordinates.precision: Approximate attraction point from the existing Kawagoe route guide

photo.alt: Exterior of Kawagoe Castle Honmaru Palace

stops.name: Kurazukuri old town ? Ichibangai
stops.address: Kurazukuri Street, Saiwaicho, Kawagoe, Saitama, Japan
stops.story: Follow the merchant street at roofline level. The thick, plastered storehouses and their substantial shutters speak to the wealth of a trading town?and the need to protect it from fire. Browse the working shops, then look for quieter side lanes where the buildings are easier to read.

coordinates.precision: Approximate street point from the existing Kawagoe route guide

photo.alt: Traditional kurazukuri storehouses along Kawagoe old town street

stops.name: Toki no Kane ? Bell of Time
stops.address: Toki no Kane, 15-7 Saiwaicho, Kawagoe, Saitama, Japan
stops.story: The town?s familiar silhouette is also a living timekeeper. The bell rings four times a day?6:00, noon, 3:00 and 6:00. Stand back from the tower, take in the adjoining kura fa?ades, and let the sound place you in the middle of a working shopping district.

coordinates.precision: Photograph location and approximate point cross-checked with Wikimedia Commons geodata

photo.alt: Toki no Kane bell tower above Kawagoe?s old town

stops.name: Kashiya Yokocho ? Candy Alley
stops.address: Kashiya Yokocho, 2-chome Motomachi, Kawagoe, Saitama 350-0062, Japan
stops.story: End where Kawagoe?s food story becomes tangible. Around 30 confectionery shops line this small lane; look for traditional candies, rice crackers and sweet-potato treats. Stores are independent, so the lane?s mood and what is open depend on the day.

coordinates.precision: Approximate lane point from the existing Kawagoe route guide

photo.alt: Traditional confectionery lane of Kashiya Yokocho in Kawagoe
